questions.q: What is the core idea behind AI-assisted human oversight?
options: Replacing the human reviewer entirely with an AI judge
Training a single model to oversee itself with no external input
Keeping a human as the final decision-maker while giving them AI-generated tools, such as critique or summarization, to extend what they can actually check
Waiting until debate and recursive reward modeling are fully solved before doing any oversight at all
questions.explain: AI-assisted human oversight is a practical, near-term category of tools that extend a human reviewer's reach without removing the human from the final decision.

questions.q: What did OpenAI's 'Self-Critiquing Models for Assisting Human Evaluators' study find?
options: Smaller models always wrote more helpful critiques than larger models
Critiques only worked on image classification tasks, not text summarization
AI-written critiques helped human labelers catch flaws in summaries that they missed without assistance, including deliberately planted misleading flaws
AI-written critiques had no measurable effect on what human labelers caught
questions.explain: The study found critiques measurably helped labelers catch more flaws, including planted misleading ones, and that larger models tended to write more helpful critiques.

questions.q: What role do summarization and fact-checking tools play in this lesson's framing of AI-assisted oversight?
options: They act as force multipliers that make review of large or technical material tractable, or catch specific factual errors, without themselves making the final quality call
They fully replace the need for any human judgment about quality
They are only useful for translating text between languages
They eliminate the need for any evaluation metrics whatsoever
questions.explain: Summarization makes otherwise-impractical review tractable, and fact-checking catches specific errors, but neither substitutes for the human's overall judgment about the work's quality.

questions.q: What new problem does handing a human reviewer an AI assistant create?
options: It makes the review process illegal in most jurisdictions

It relocates the trust problem onto the assistant itself — if the assistant is subtly wrong in ways the human can't detect, the human's confidence can rise without actual reliability improving to match
It requires the human reviewer to have no domain expertise at all
It eliminates the trust problem entirely since AI assistants are always accurate
questions.explain: Giving a human an AI assistant doesn't remove the question of trustworthiness — it shifts that question onto whether the assistant itself can be trusted.

questions.q: How does this lesson frame the relationship between debate, recursive reward modeling, weak-to-strong generalization, and AI-assisted human oversight?
options: As four mutually exclusive techniques where only one can ever be correct
As four unrelated topics that happen to appear in the same chapter by coincidence
As a strict chronological sequence where each technique fully replaces the one before it

As overlapping angles on the same underlying scalable oversight problem, none of which fully solves it alone — for example, a debate with a human judge is itself a structured case of AI-assisted oversight
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties the four proposals together as overlapping, complementary attempts at the same problem rather than competing final answers.
